newsitem.title: GERMANY: German debt stumbles in line with U.S. market.
newsitem.headline: German debt stumbles in line with U.S. market.

text.p: German debt was kicked lower in late session trading on Tuesday by stronger than expected U.S. economic data and dealers said the next days' direction would largely depend on the U.S. market's close.

Trading down 38 basis points at 99.82 just before the close, the March futures contract had fallen swiftly in afternoon trading from its session high of 100.16, hit in morning trading. At the same time the April 2006 cash bond was trading at 102.38, compared with Monday's 102.67 close.
"The market was clearly sucked lower by softer Treasuries reacting to the stronger November data," a dealer said.
Although the market was trading lower much of the morning, price drops accelerated shortly after U.S. November housing starts, measuring a stronger than expected 1.514 million, were released.
Traders feared the numbers showed more resilience in the economy, raising fears the U.S. central bank may be inclined to raise interest rates soon. The Fed board meets on Tuesday.
Even a French interest rate cut, where the intervention rate was moved to 3.15 percent from 3.20 percent, failed to support the German market, dealers said.
But dealers said the French move should not fan speculation that the Bundesbank may follow suit at its year-end policy-setting council meeting on Thursday.
They added the fact that the council will hold a news conference after Thursday's meeting also does not give hints about any possible rate changes.
"It would be wrong to assume the Bundesbank may be prompted to nudge the repo rate lower on Thursday," a dealer said.
The central bank will discuss its money supply target on Thursday and traditionally holds a news conference after this meeting to explain the target to the public.
Noting that the U.S. market will likely to be highly influential for the German debt market in the next sessions, dealers predicted Bunds could trade between 99 and 101 before the year end.
